cells.tense: You're keeping the aim and staying open to what you feel on the way to it.
cells.ask: Pick one aim you're moving on, name out loud one feeling you have about it, and let someone answer before you go back to the plan.
cells.core:
You've got a direction and you're moving on it, and the aim hasn't closed you off. That's the harder combination, and it's the one you're running. Something stays open while the rest of you pushes, so you catch the feel of a thing before you can say what to do about it.

The pull to gather every possible feeling — yours, theirs, what the room might hold — sits close enough to the edge that it has to stay a choice made on purpose. Nothing needs pouring into the open part yet; it can just stay open. The ask below takes a minute and doesn't touch the plan.
cells.sheetLine: You're moving on something and still letting it reach you.
cells.verb: opening to feel something before it has a name
cells.place: in the push toward a goal you're already moving on

cells.tense: You're bracing for what this will feel like once it lands, ahead of the thing landing.
cells.ask: Take the next step on one goal today and only plan the step after it once it's done — no further.
cells.core:
Run well, this looks like moving on a goal until it's finished and only then letting yourself feel about it. The step lands clean because nothing was riding on it in advance, and what you feel afterward has room to be news.

What happens instead: you keep aiming at how it'll feel when it's over. Before the next step, you've rehearsed the receiving — the approval, the letdown, the way you'll arrange your face. You push past the timing that would have made the step land right, and the motion spends itself on a future you can't write in. The trouble isn't feeling. It's settling the verdict before the thing is finished. One step, then look up.
cells.sheetLine: You keep rehearsing the landing before you've moved.

cells.tense: The push is running and the place that lets a new thing reach you is quiet.
cells.ask: Name one thing you want that has no plan attached yet, and say it out loud to one person today without adding what you'd do about it.
cells.core:
Run well, this is moving toward something while still able to want a thing you can't plan yet — the wanting comes first and the direction follows, so the aim keeps taking new shape as you go.

Where you stand now, the direction is there and the wanting isn't. You move on what's already decided, and the moment before a thing had a name — the part where you just feel it out — you stopped standing in it. So every push keeps its old shape, and nothing new gets let in. You arrive once the moment has passed. The way back is the smallest move there is: want something before you know what to do with it. No plan comes off it.
cells.sheetLine: You arrive after the moment has passed, not into it.

cells.tense: The move back toward what's fair is already happening, and you call it keeping things even.
cells.ask: In one exchange today, take what's offered without adding anything back to square it, and say thank you once.
cells.core:
Run well, this is feeling what's fair and moving toward it without keeping score — give and take flow, and neither needs a ledger because the exchange is trusted to come back around.

The moving part you already do. You feel what's fair and you take the step toward it, and it costs effort you don't tally. Where it goes unseen: you describe it as though everybody just happens to be reasonable, or as though the evenness keeps itself. That keeps the turn invisible, and the turn is yours. Tonight, don't level it. Let one thing arrive uneven and stay that way.
cells.sheetLine: The turning toward fair already happens, and you're not counting it as yours.
